title: Acoustic learning maps spider-monkey associations with forest disturbance
summary: A learned call detector, manual confirmation and occupancy modeling analyzed recordings from 341 Costa Rican sites. In this sample, Geoffroy's spider monkey was detected only above 80% forest cover and away from nearby primary paved roads. These are regional observational associations, not causal or universal habitat thresholds; imperfect detection and the focus on one call type limit inference.

evidence.tested: Model positives from field recordings were manually checked and linked to landscape observations.
evidence.unknown: Causality, independent ground-truth survey agreement and transfer to other regions were not established.
evidence.ai_role: Attention-equipped residual convolutional call detector supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Primary article dates, affiliations and selected detector Methods, Results and limitations; supplement not reviewed.
